summary: Michihiko Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1964–1974). He served as an assistant (attested 1978–1980) and professor (~1995–2015) at Taisho University, with affiliations at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute and the Japanese Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies.

Michihiko Yajima works in Indology and Buddhist studies. A former graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981), he held a post there (attested 1992) and later served as a professor at Tsurumi Women's University (attested 2003).

Michihiro Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held teaching posts at Setagaya Gakuen High School (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), and served as a librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005).

Michiko Yusa works in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. She completed her doctoral studies under Raimon Panikkar (~1979–1983) and served as a professor in the Department of Foreign Languages at Western Washington University (~1983–2020).

Michio Kamikawa was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University (~1979–1988) and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University from around 1995 to 2021.

Michio Yano is an Indologist and historian. He studied at Kyoto University (~1963–1996) under Kiyoshi Yabuuchi, and at Brown University under David Pingree (~1978–1979). From 1973 to 2015, he was a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University.

Michitaro Tanaka was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University under Hidenaka Tanaka (~1923–1926). He held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1947–1950) and Ryukoku University, and taught Takeshi Umehara.

Michitoshi Baraida is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi. He held posts at Otani University, Toho Gakuin, Toho Kenkyukai, and the Eastern Institute as chief priest of Ganshō-ji.
Michiya Ito was a graduate student at Tohoku University (attested 1986–1990) and later held an academic post there (attested 2001–2004).
Michiyo Hoshi is a researcher in Tibetology and linguistics. She held posts as a joint researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 2003) and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
Midori Nishino is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006) and later worked there as a researcher (attested 2010–2015).

Migmar Tsering was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences, and served as head of Sakya College.

Mihai Șora was a philosopher who studied at the University of Bucharest under Mircea Eliade, the University of Paris, and CNRS. He held a post at the State Publishing House for Literature and Arts (~1957–1969).

Mikaël Bauer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Noritoshi Aramaki and Paul Hoornaert, and earned his PhD at Harvard under Ryuichi Abe. He is an associate professor at McGill University.

Mikel Burley is a philosopher and Indologist. He studied at the University of Essex under Jay M. Bernstein, at the University of Bristol under John Peacock, and also under Jonardon Ganeri and Brian Carr. He joined the University of Leeds.
Miki Ujiie is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied abroad at Tribhuvan University. He held an instructional post at Koyasan University (attested 1970).
Mikio Otsuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Attested in 2007, he held appointments as a professor at Hanazono University and as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji.

Mikisaburo Mori was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology. He earned degrees from Kyoto University and Osaka University, and held posts at the Kyoto Institute of the Academy of Oriental Culture, Osaka High School, Osaka University, and Bukkyo University.
Milman Parry was a linguist who studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet. He held an academic post at Harvard University from around 1929 until 1935.

Milton Singer was a scholar in Indology and other fields. He studied at the University of Texas at Austin (~1930–1936) and the University of Chicago (~1936–1940), where he subsequently held a faculty post from around 1940 to 1979.
